contexts.text: In their vernal flower and smile.

(Abraham) laughed () = the affection of truth; as may be evident from the origin and essence of laughter. Its origin is nothing else than the affection of truth, or the affection of falsity. Hence come hilarity and gladness, which put themselves forth in the face by means of laughter. Hence it is evident that the essence of laughter is nothing else. Laughter, indeed, is a something external, which is of the body, because of the face; but in the Word interior things are expressed and signified by means of exterior ones... thus the affection of truth by laughter. In the Rational of man there is truth, which is the chief thing. There is also the affection of good in it; but this affection is in the affection of truth itself, as its soul. The affection of good which is in the Rational does not put itself forth by laughter; but by a certain joy; and by a derivative delight of pleasure which does not laugh; for in laughter there is commonly something which is not so good...

That laughter here = the affection of truth, may be evident from the fact that it is here mentioned that Abraham laughed; and in like manner Sarah, both before Isaac was born, and also after he was born; and also from Isaac's having been named from laughter; for Isaac means laughter. Illustrated.
Because laughter, in the internal sense, = the affection of truth, which is of the Rational... thus, here, the Divine Rational.
That the human rational truth with the Lord did not perceive it, thus did not believe, is signified by the laughter of Sarah at the door of the tent, which was behind him.
Sarah laughed within herself () = the affection of truth of that Rational, that it should be so. To laugh, or laughter, = the affection of truth.
Why did Sarah laugh at this? () = the thought of rational truth from its affection. To laugh, or laughter = the affection which is of truth.
Sarah denied, saying, I did not laugh, because she was afraid () = that human rational truth wanted to excuse itself...

He said, Nay, but thou didst laugh () = that still it was such... How these things are circumstanced, may be evident from those things which have been said above concerning the signification of to laugh, or of laughter; namely, that it is an affection of the Rational; and in fact the affection of truth or of falsity in the Rational. Thence is all laughter. So long as there is such an affection in the Rational as puts itself forth in laughter, so long there is something corporeal and worldly, thus merely human. Celestial good and spiritual good does not laugh; but it brings out its delight and cheerfulness in the face, speech, and gesture, in a different way. For there are very many things in laughter; as, for the most part, something of contempt; which, although it does not appear, still lies hidden; and it easily distinguishes itself from that cheerfulness of the lower mind, which also produces something like laughter. The state of the human Rational with the Lord is described by Sarah's laughing; and by it there is signified with what affection the truth of the Rational regarded that which was said; [namely] that it was to be put off, and the Divine put on; not that it laughed; but that it perceived from the Divine of what quality it still was, and how much of the human there was still in it that had to be expelled. This is signified, in the internal sense, by the laughter of Sarah.
(Sarah said) God hath made me laugh () = the affection of celestial truth. Laughter = the affection of truth.
Everyone who heareth shall laugh to me () = that all things there will have affection.
That to laugh = to be affected with truth; or to have the affection of truth. References.
Laughter, from which Isaac was named, = the affection of truth, or the good of truth.
Behold Isaac laughing with Rebekah his woman () = that Divine good was present in Divine truth; or that Divine good was adjoined to Divine truth... To laugh = the love or affection of truth.
The Spirits of Jupiter... disposed the face to be smiling and cheerful.
They were pleased with the faces... which were cheerful and smiling.

The reason they were pleased with the smiling and cheerful faces, was that in their Earth the faces of almost all are such; and this because they have no solicitude about future things, nor have they worldly cares.
Even if, with those who are not good, there is cheerfulness and laughter in the face, it is in the external skin; and not in the fibres from the internal.
He laughs at everything of the Church...
Hence all things before their eyes as it were laugh, play, and are alive.
It can then laugh at those things.
In their hearts they have laughed at the holy things of the Church.
In a smile of cheerfulness.
The Angels... smiled.
At this they all laughed, and said...
At this our host laughed most heartily - toto pectore.
(The Angels) smiled pleasantly.
In (the cry) there was something of laughter; and in this something of indignation; and in this something of sadness. TCR 694.
At this, the three new-comers said, smiling...
He then listened, but smiling. TCR 35:8.
At this they laughed.
On seeing this portent, the bystanders laughed with a loud laugh.
At this they laughed, saying, You are joking.
I could no longer restrain my laughter.
Then, sometimes they laugh at those things.
When a hypocritical preacher returns home, he laughs at all the things... he has said.
Some of the Spirits laugh at such things... they laugh that they are so; and they laugh because it is said that the last times are at hand.
The Spirits... laughed through me.
From whatever affection they are thinking; as from... a laugh... in that thing there may lie hidden many things which are simultaneously in it, or present with it...
A place where were those who were laughing together.
At wasteness and famine thou shalt laugh. Explained.
They laugh when they hear...
The Angels with a smile asked them.
